subject: MSA redlines: clarifying output ownership and feedback-license delegation
messages:
From: Sara Matthews <sara.matthews@acmelegal.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com; procurement@atlascare.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasCare MSA redlines (output / training concerns)

Laura — attached are the redlines AtlasCare legal uploaded after our internal review. The two main items are: (1) a carveout that would prevent Redwood from using any customer-provided content to further train models that power features sold to AtlasCare (they want a strict opt-in); and (2) language on derivative/attribution that would require AtlasCare to be identified as a source if generated outputs are used in AtlasCare product marketing.

We flagged a few optional mitigations in the comments: a narrowly scoped feedback license (time- and model-limited), telemetry-only telemetry terms, and a paragraph on anonymized, aggregated training signals. AtlasCare’s procurement team wants to avoid broad "training consent" language.

Please see annotations page 4-6 for the exact requested substitutions. Let me know if Redwood has precedent language for (a) a timebox (e.g., 12 months) on feedback/training license and (b) an attribution carveout that doesn't require product-level brand attribution.

Best,
Sara Matthews
Senior Counsel, Acme Legal (external counsel for AtlasCare)
Attachments: AtlasCare_MSA_redlines_20261006.docx, AtlasCare_Redline_annotated.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: AtlasCare MSA redlines (output / training concerns)

Sara — thanks for the redlines and the clear notes. Looping in Karthik (legal ops), Marcus (product counsel) and Kim (customer success/legal) for input. High-level response from Redwood: we are sympathetic to AtlasCare’s desire for control over their content; our ask is to preserve the ability to improve model safety and performance at a platform level, and to avoid per-customer constraints that would require separate model binaries or costly isolation that materially increases latency/cost.

Initial thoughts: 
- Feedback license: we can accept a limited feedback license, but propose 12-month timebox + prohibition on training on raw customer PII. We suggest language that allows use of derived, aggregated signals for quality improvements and safety fixes.
- Training opt-out carveout: if AtlasCare wants a hard opt-out for model retraining, we can offer an isolated variant path (Dedicated/Private deployment) as an alternative commercial term, but that would change pricing.
- Attribution: we cannot accept automatic marketing attribution for generated outputs (this materially impacts product UX & downstream publisher expectations). We can offer a narrow attribution right for materials that use AtlasCare brand verbatim in marketing collateral, subject to pre-approval.

Can the AtlasCare team confirm which of these approaches they'd prefer (limited license vs opt-out + dedicated deployment)? Happy to propose concrete contract language once we have direction.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: AtlasCare MSA redlines (output / training concerns)

Sara / Laura — draft compromise language below that I think is operationally implementable and narrow enough to satisfy AtlasCare concerns. I pasted the proposed clauses inline for easy review.

--- Proposed feedback/training license clause (redacted for thread) ---
"Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Customer Content solely to generate aggregated and anonymized signals for the purpose of improving the performance, safety and reliability of Redwood’s inference platform (\"Quality Signals\"). Use of Customer Content for model re-training that would update weights of a general-purpose shared model is excluded unless Customer provides express, written consent. This license shall automatically expire twelve (12) months from the date Customer Content is first received by Redwood."

--- Proposed attribution/derivative clause ---
"Redwood shall not be required to attribute AtlasCare for outputs generated by the Service in customer applications. Where AtlasCare elects to reproduce or publicize a Generated Output that includes AtlasCare Confidential Information or proprietary marks, AtlasCare shall obtain Redwood’s prior written consent for use of Redwood trademarks and, conversely, Redwood will not be required to attribute AtlasCare in its product marketing except where AtlasCare’s brand or logos are used verbatim and subject to AtlasCare approval."

Rationale / implementation notes: 
- The training clause blocks blanket weight-updates on shared models and permits only anonymized, aggregated signals for platform-level improvements. That avoids per-customer model forks.
- The 12-month sunset addresses their ask for a timebox. 
- If AtlasCare needs full opt-out (no signals at all), we should follow Laura’s note and offer a Dedicated or Private deployment priced differently; we should flag this to sales since it impacts margin.

Marcus / Kim — any redlines to the proposed wording before I share it with Sara? If not, I can convert this into tracked-change language and send via DocuSign or Google Doc for AtlasCare counsel review.

Thanks,
Karthik
Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
